title: THE RULE BOOK
premise: ME, CLYDE & 1 MISSING RULE BOOK. EXOTICCENZO and his best friend CLYDE find only the gutted cover and one page of an old man's Rule Book (everyone thinks it is a trading book), and hunt its pages across the world. They believe it has 99 pages. Episodes 1-100 are THE SEARCH: the complete Rule Book is found at exactly Episode 100, where they discover it really has 884 pages. Episode 101 onward is PART TWO: discovering and understanding the book now in their hands, and it never concludes.
rules_for_daily_scripts: STORY FIRST. This is an adventure about EXOTICCENZO, Clyde and 1 missing Rule Book: the hunt for pages, Solo's race, Mtoriro's missing uncle. Plot, friendships, places and jokes lead every episode. It is never a trading class. Viewer ideas and trends add to the story and never replace it.

THE 100-EPISODE PLAN. Chapters are exactly 10 episodes and follow masterplan.chapters. Every episode moves the hunt forward with a page or clue. By Episode 100 they have travelled the whole world by train, plane and ship. Number collected pages in order. Everyone believes the book has 99 pages. The final piece is found in their Zimbabwe homeland at exactly Episode 100, not before; the complete book has 884 pages. Episode 100 delivers the most powerful lesson of the series and changes more than 100 characters on screen. Episode 101 onward is about discovering and understanding the book, and the story never concludes.

THE LESSON. From Episode 16 every lesson is a LIFE RULE, never trading or betting: money habits, friends, love and family, work, pride, patience, habits, saying no, honesty. Only EXOTICCENZO explains it, but anyone can cause or learn it: Clyde, friends, strangers, gym regulars, shopkeepers, kombi drivers, fans. It comes from a random, funny, unexpected moment. Viewers must not guess it until EXOTICCENZO breaks it down at the end. Vary the format. Write moments so true to everyday life that viewers feel they are watching their own reality. In the story, the Rule Book is the Prof's rules for life; the trading pages were a disguise (see plot_threads, book_truth).

OPENING. Set a short shock hook on screen. The first spoken line is conflict or stakes, never scene-setting. Every episode must make sense alone, so give new viewers the setup in the first or second line without a slow recap.

PACING. Whole video 20-25 seconds including the end card: 6-8 lines, each under 40 characters. Start mid-action in shot 1 (someone already running, grabbing, shouting) so frame 1 works with the sound off. A joke or surprise by second 8, another near 15. Change something every 2 to 4 seconds. Vary the structure between episodes (chase, argument, text-message gag, list, silent gag) so the feed never sees the same template twice in a row.

ENDING. Close on a cliffhanger that pays off next episode, mostly an open question; cut mid-action only when the next episode truly delivers. Then the outro: EXOTICCENZO alone, thanking viewers or telling a fresh joke that comes out of this episode's unexpected moment, about whoever caused it, never spoiling a hidden hint. All end screens must fit this episode's story. No song credit. Every video loops: it cuts back to the opening shot with the hook, so write the last line to flow into the first.

WORLD AND CAST. EXOTICCENZO and Clyde live together in Zimbabwe, between Harare and Bulawayo. Home is the base and the most-used setting. Every few episodes they travel abroad by train, plane or ship, then return home. Everyday scenes are constant: eating, games, sofas, kombis, shops, the gym, phones, jobs, family visits. Every place is full of ordinary people going about their lives. Give background people moments of their own when funny. Characters talk like friends. Add a new recurring character every chapter or two, and bring old ones back.

THE VIBE. EXOTICCENZO and Clyde are permanently chilled, shown only by red eyes and jokes: sleepy, hungry, Clyde forgetting what he was saying. Shady dealers exist in the world, in dark alleys and, unexpectedly, in nice houses (sets alley, villa), but keep it implied: only unmarked packages, whispers and the word dealer. Never show, name or refer to weed, smoking or any drug by name in the video, caption or hashtags.

GLOW-UP. Appearance changes automatically every 10 episodes from Episode 11: EXOTICCENZO gets bigger and more cut; Clyde barely changes, just slightly taller than Cenzo. One or two gym episodes each chapter, starting Episodes 8-10, so it feels earned. Gym scenes still move the hunt forward.
FANS. Commenters can become recurring side characters. Roles are positive or friendly-funny; never mock them, make them villains or let them teach.

CAPTIONS AND SEARCH. The first words name the everyday life problem people search, such as Can't say no to friends? or Always broke before payday? A character says it out loud, and the hook or rule card shows it. Ask an easy question such as Yes or no? Use 2 or 3 specific life hashtags (e.g. #liferules #lifelessons #adulting), ending with #stickman, never #fyp, #viral or trading tags. Write at least one line per episode someone would send to a friend. Put the episode number and series name in the caption (e.g. THE RULE BOOK Ep 16). End the caption with an A/B choice about what happens next or what the viewer would do (e.g. Paris or home next? A or B?), not a generic yes or no, so Vincenzo can pin a comment poll with the same options; when the comments pick a path, the episode says 'you chose this'.
SAFETY. No profit promises, no specific buy or sell calls, and no paid-service adverts until Vincenzo turns them back on.

THE LONG GAME. Each chapter sets up one thing viewers expect at its start, then something unexpected happens at the last moment in its final episodes. Across the chapter, plant small hidden hints in the background or in throwaway lines that viewers will not notice. Characters seen in separate episodes later turn out to be connected. In the payoff, EXOTICCENZO links the hints together: it becomes a lesson nobody saw coming and uncovers a Rule Book clue. Record the planned twist and each hint in series.json plot_threads with its episode, and pay every one off.

LOOKS. Every 20 episodes, EXOTICCENZO's and Clyde's outfits change automatically: EXOTICCENZO in a Future-inspired style, Clyde in a Gunna-inspired style, generic with no real logos. Other characters wear random outfits by era, and background people dress for the place they are in, so research what is worn there when building a new country. Everyone stands on the ground in a place that makes sense.

LANGUAGE. Abroad, characters still speak English (the global audience reads the big English captions); add tr to each line's options so the local-language version shows as a small subtitle above the speaker. No speech bubbles. Zimbabwe scenes stay in English. Spoken voices stay English.

STYLE: From Episode 15 every episode renders in the illustrated cartoon style automatically (big-head stickmen in real clothes, close-ups on the speaker, one-word captions). Keep lines punchy and conversational so the word-by-word captions read well. Do not set a style in scripts.

CHARACTER BRAND (from top animated creators: Kapinto, Tegwolo, Bob Kichwa Ngumu). Fixed traits, never drift: CLYDE is the over-confident schemer whose big plan always backfires; EXOTICCENZO is the deadpan, red-eyed one who is always right without trying. Clyde's catchphrase when a plan starts: 'TRUST ME, I HAVE A PLAN.' EXOTICCENZO's catchphrase on the rule card: 'ANOTHER PAGE. ANOTHER RULE.' Use each at most once per episode, and keep them word-for-word so viewers can quote them.

LANGUAGE AND RELATABILITY. Write for a global English-speaking audience first: everyday situations anyone gets (broke before payday, group chats, crushes, bosses, family, food, phones, load-shedding-style power cuts). Zimbabwe stays home base and gives flavour (kombis, sadza, aunties, ZESA), but jokes must land for viewers who have never been there. Slang mix per episode (see slang.json): 2-4 current American Gen Z terms, used naturally and never more than one per line; at most 1-2 Zimbabwean words, only where context or the picture makes the meaning obvious. Voices: CLYDE leans hardest into American slang and uses it slightly wrong for laughs (he's trying too hard); EXOTICCENZO is calm, plain-spoken, with an occasional 'sharp sharp' or 'eish'. Side characters can use more Shona or Ndebele. Never use anything on slang.json's avoid list.

FAN RULES. About once a week, ask in the caption: 'Drop a rule the book should have.' Turn the most-liked comment into a 'FAN RULE' page in a later episode, credit the @username in the caption, and keep it positive.

BACKGROUND (from Gravity Falls, Rick and Morty, Skibidi Toilet, Bob's Burgers). The renderer already makes outdoor crowds freeze, turn and film on their phones on shock/angry lines, and hides BUCKET HAT GUY (orange bucket hat, green shirt) in every outdoor crowd. In scripts: (1) seed a future character as a background cameo 1-3 episodes before they matter; (2) once per chapter, hide a silent story clue in a background action and pay it off later ('rewind ep N'); (3) about every 5th episode, let a caption or outro wink at Bucket Hat Guy ('spot him?') without explaining him; (4) keep extras plain so the leads always stand out. The renderer also shows a PUN SIGN that changes every episode (signs.json; add new jokes at the end, never delete) and the REGULARS, the same background people in the same spots every time: the kombi tout (red cap, orange vest, Harare and the station), the aunty with the shopping bag (purple doek, Harare and Bulawayo), the fruit vendor (Bulawayo and the station) and the baguette man (Paris). A regular can be promoted to a speaking side character when the story needs one; give them a name and add them to characters and voices.py.

cenzo.name: EXOTICCENZO
cenzo.bio: The main man. Calm, sharp, loyal. Learns by doing.

clyde.name: CLYDE
clyde.bio: Best friend. Always hungry, always all-in, loyal to the end.

nia.name: MTORIRO
nia.bio: From Harare. His uncle wrote the Rule Book and vanished. Holds the book's history, but leaves the teaching to Cenzo.

zeke.name: SOLO
zeke.bio: Rival page hunter. Works alone. Polished, smug, always one step ahead.

maya.name: JAMAL
maya.bio: Tokyo-based creator who films everything. Knows every shortcut.

ruva.name: RUVA
ruva.bio: Air hostess from Harare. Warm, quick, knows everyone's name before they say it. Flies the Tokyo route.

gogo.name: GOGO
gogo.bio: Grandmother on the Bulawayo night train. Sleeps like a queen, wakes like thunder. Somehow knows Ruva.

moyo.name: MR MOYO
moyo.bio: Ruva's sleepy neighbour from Bulawayo. Paid to nap on planes as the decoy 'old man'. Friendly, slow, always yawning.

tino.name: MAI TINO
tino.bio: Harare street vendor outside the uncle's old shop. Sells anything in a box, loud and kind, counts to three for every sale.

antoine.name: ANTOINE
antoine.bio: Paris cafe waiter at Cafe Le Haut. Polite, deadpan, has worked the same terrace for twenty years and remembers every customer who ever asked nicely.

plot_threads.expect: Find Mtoriro's uncle by following Solo home to Zimbabwe.
plot_threads.twist: Episode 9-10: Ruva is the uncle's daughter. She has been helping him hide from Solo, and the 'old man' Solo sat beside on the plane was a decoy. Her hints link to a Rule Book clue in Bulawayo.

hints.hint: Ruva calls Clyde by name though nobody told her it.
Ruva says the old man 'slept' the whole flight while Solo copied his notebook: a decoy never shows his face.
Ruva texts Cenzo's phone though he never gave her his number, and she knows the Bulawayo train time.
Gogo on the night train says Ruva told her Clyde would be loud: Ruva planned their trip and asked Gogo to wake them.

plot_threads.paid_off_note: Ep 10: Ruva revealed as the uncle's daughter; Mr Moyo was the paid decoy 'old man'; Solo copied a fake notebook; Gogo woke them for Ruva; Bulawayo clue = page 3.

plot_threads.expect: Find out why Solo signed page 3 and track the uncle, then follow the trail to Paris.
plot_threads.twist: Planned for Episodes 19-20: Solo and Ruva's father co-wrote the first pages years ago; Solo's signature is a partner's, not a thief's. He hunts the book to finish what they started. Links to a Paris clue.

hints.hint: Mai Tino sells 'the old man and his PARTNER's boxes': the uncle had a partner.
Solo's locker photo shows the uncle beside a man whose face is cut out (it is young Solo).
Solo whispers 'Sorry, old friend' to the photo as he walks away.
Page 5 (signed Paris) calls the uncle 'LE PROF', a nickname only his old partner used; Solo should later slip and say 'Prof'.
Solo slips and calls the uncle 'the Prof' on the plane (page 5's nickname for him) and knows his hiding habits: 'always hid things high'.
Antoine the Paris waiter: 'A man in a suit asked too. Years ago.' Young Solo came to Cafe Le Haut with the Prof.
Antoine's old Cafe Le Haut bill: two coffees, LE PROF and 'S' (Solo).

plot_threads.note: Plant 3-4 hints in eps 11-18 (e.g. Solo knows an old nickname for the uncle; an old photo with two men in the background).

plot_threads.reveal: In Paris, page 6 (hidden up high, as Solo said) shows the Rule Book is the Prof's rules for LIFE: money, friends, family, work, pride. The trading pages were a disguise so greedy hunters like Solo would chase charts and miss what the book really is. Cenzo reads it first; Clyde is disappointed there are no 'money cheat codes', then laughs. From here every rule card is a life rule.
plot_threads.keep: Solo still believes it is a trading book that will make him rich; do not tell him yet. Keep the Solo-and-the-Prof partner reveal for eps 19-20 (Solo co-wrote the early 'trading' disguise pages).
plot_threads.revealed: Ep 16: page 6 on Antoine's top shelf at Cafe Le Haut reads 'Rules for life. Not money.' Clyde: 'No money cheat codes?! Ha!'

weekly_learnings.window: Episodes 1-14, posted 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (956 views, 4 follows). Small sample: every video got 32-91 views, so treat these as working bets, not proven rules.
rules: FIRST LINE = A PERSONAL CONFESSION OR DEMAND ANYONE GETS WITHOUT LORE. Short, first person, about money or food or pride ('I PUT ALL MY MONEY ON ONE TRADE.', 'THAT PHOTO IS MINE. GIVE IT BACK.'). Keep lore names out of line 1 (the Rule Book's writer, Solo signing pages, page numbers). Data: eps 1, 2, 3, 13, 14 kept 44-57% of viewers at 3 seconds; lore-first eps 6, 7, 8, 11 kept 28-38%.

LAND THE FIRST SURPRISE BY SECOND 8, NOT 15. Only 6-16% of viewers are still watching at 10 seconds, so the 15-second surprise is seen by almost nobody. Keep the 15-second one too, but add an earlier twist or punchline.
KEEP THE VIDEO UNDER 32 SECONDS. Runtime crept to 34-35 seconds by eps 9-13 and finish rate fell to 0-2.6%, against 3.7-7.2% for the 28-32 second eps 1-3. Cut a line rather than run long.
